- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust up by 1–3% if price is trending down.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of mean-reversion (price moving back toward 30-day average), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ days), model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If true outcome is consistently above forecast, model may be underestimating sentiment-driven momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is positive and price is rising.
